system_description.narrative_title: A Fracturing Order: War, Tech Shock and Energy-Strained Alliances
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an interlinked, open system under stress from simultaneous shocks: regional wars and mediation efforts (notably Iran and Ukraine) that threaten trade and energy flows; a tech and financial upheaval driven by AI spending, a massive crypto heist and market routs; and political fragmentation in key democracies that weakens policy coordination. These processes amplify one another through supply-chain, capital-market and cyber linkages, producing cascading risks across energy, finance, and security domains while creating space for new alignments and mediation efforts.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, regional security theatres (Middle East, Black Sea/Ukraine), major multinational firms (tech, energy, finance), global markets (equities, bonds, crypto), mediators and international organisations, supply chains, cyber and information domains, and public/political opinion dynamics shaping policy.
system_description.super_system: The global international political-economic order (the interconnected system of state actors, markets, institutions and transnational flows that governs world affairs).
adjacent_subsystems: International financial and capital markets (including crypto infrastructure)

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, with NATO and EU support, are locked in an extended military contest whose shifting frontlines and political alignments continue to reshape European security and deterrence patterns.

variables.name: US–Iran standoff and mediation
variables.description: The United States and Iran, alongside regional actors and mediators, are oscillating between diplomatic engagement and military escalation as negotiations and strikes risk redefining power and influence across the Gulf and Levant.

variables.name: US–China technological and economic rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are contesting leadership in critical technologies, supply chains and economic influence — from semiconductors and AI to telecoms and data infrastructure — producing persistent trade, investment and regulatory friction.

variables.name: Global market turbulence and capital reallocation
variables.description: Major central banks, investors and governments are navigating a period of heightened financial volatility driven by sector-specific corrections and tighter policy, which is reallocating capital and altering the economic leverage of states and corporations worldwide.

variables.name: State-linked cyber thefts and crypto-enabled sanctions evasion
variables.description: Nation-state actors — most prominently North Korea — are using cyber operations and cryptocurrency channels to steal assets and evade sanctions, undermining financial integrity and forcing changes in sanctions enforcement and cross-border cyber norms.
